posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
I went through your ( 22f3001617) code, it has logical issues.

Here are the key issues in the solution:

Major Logical Errors

The for(i=1; i<=NR; i++) loop is completely wrong

  • NR is the number of records read so far, not the number of fields or characters in the current line.
  • This loop repeats the check NR times for each line.
  • If the current line is 0, count_0 increments NR times, inflating the count exponentially.

Example:
If there are 4 lines and only the first is 0, final count_0 will be:

Line 1: NR=1 → count_0 += 1
Line 2: NR=2 → count_0 += 2
Line 3: NR=3 → count_0 += 3
Line 4: NR=4 → count_0 += 4
Total = 1+2+3+4 = 10 (instead of 1)

Using IFS="\n" does nothing in awk

  • IFS is a shell variable.
  • Awk uses FS (Field Separator), not IFS.
  • And here each line is already the whole record, so setting FS isn’t even needed.

The probability calculation is wrong

prob = count_0 / NR — but due to error #1, count_0 is not counting zeros correctly.

Minor Mistakes

  • ((count_0++)) has unnecessary parentheses — count_0++ is enough.

What you should have done instead

Increment counts once per line:

{
  sum+= $0
}

END{
  if (sum/NR > 0.5) {
    print "not"
  } else {
    print "naught"
  }
}

Summary

Issue Description
Wrong Loop Counts each zero multiple times based on NR
Redundant Variable Uses IFS does nothing, as it is not awk variable
Wrong Logic Probability becomes meaningless
Unnecessary Complexity Overthinking what is a simple condition
